title: Stop Burning Tokens: Why self-improvement needs domain expertise first - Annabell Schäfer, Langfuse
talk_summary: The talk describes a minimal self-optimization loop for a classification task, showing that high-signal yes/no feedback plus held-out validation beats vague LLM-judge scores. It argues that domain expertise should be encoded early as concrete failure modes, examples, evaluators, and stopping criteria so agents improve without burning tokens.

takeaways.technique: Binary domain-specific evaluators instead of vague scores
takeaways.what_they_do: They replace generic correctness/helpfulness 0-1 or 1-5 judges with concrete yes/no checks tied to domain failure modes, such as whether an answer is grounded in retrieved context or uses the correct brand voice.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of correctness the answer is based on the knowledge base yes no

takeaways.technique: Error-cluster-driven prompt updates with held-out validation
takeaways.what_they_do: On a fit set they score per item, cluster errors and confused label pairs, have a frontier optimizer propose a prompt change for the biggest error cluster, and accept it only if validation accuracy improves; the test set is untouched until the end.
takeaways.evidence_quote: on the fit data set you do this error analysis
takeaways.numbers: Baseline 68%; first iteration +10% to 78%; peaked 83%; plateau ~80%; test 80.2%; 15% total uptake; 200 fit/100 validate/300 test items.

takeaways.technique: Hard stopping criteria and escape hatch
takeaways.what_they_do: The optimization loop stops after 15 runs or at 92% accuracy and withholds the test set link until final evaluation, preventing endless token burn.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Either it's 15 runs uh completed or we have 92% accuracy reached

takeaways.technique: Add decision rules and few-shot examples for confused cases
takeaways.what_they_do: The optimizer improved a flat label list by adding a general classification approach, rules for similar classes, and examples of frequently misclassified pairs, not by adding label descriptions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: improvement loop added rules and examples

takeaways.technique: Cheap worker model plus frontier optimizer
takeaways.what_they_do: They run the production classifier on a small cheap model while using a frontier model only to analyze errors and propose prompt updates.
takeaways.evidence_quote: based on GPD5 for nano because we wanted to see how a very small and cheap model performs

takeaways.technique: Human review of production samples to refresh evals
takeaways.what_they_do: They insist on humans reviewing production data, not only coding agents, to understand shifting scope and failure modes and encode them into examples and evaluators.
takeaways.evidence_quote: review this data and don't review it only with your coding agents but review it as a human
